proposed_relationship: Combining discriminative neural networks with generative models that maximize likelihood can produce sharper samples by leveraging the strengths of both approaches.
mechanism: The mechanism behind this proposed relationship is that discriminative neural networks can provide a more accurate classification of the modes in the data distribution, while the generative models can learn to produce samples that are more realistic and diverse. By combining these two approaches, the resulting model can learn to produce samples that are not only realistic but also sharply defined, rather than blurry. This can be achieved by using the discriminative neural network to guide the generative model towards producing samples that are more likely to belong to a specific mode, rather than averaging over all modes.
constraint_released: The constraint of averaging over modes is released, allowing the model to produce more realistic and diverse samples.
